scenes.say: Does test-driven development always fit? Where can it break down?

rows.b: Add code to pass the test

scenes.say: The TDD cycle is simple. First, write a failing test. Second, write code to make it pass. Third, refactor for clarity.

scenes.label: Logic
scenes.say: Test-driven development works best for logic-heavy code, like algorithms or data processing.
But TDD struggles with user interfaces or complex integrations. It’s not a one-size-fits-all.

scenes.question: Should you always use TDD?
scenes.right: No. Adapt your approach for UI or integrations.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Should you always use TDD? No. Adapt your approach for UI or integration-heavy features.
